messages.subject: [Bug] The Report Option "-R" of featureCounts Generates Invalid Binary Characters
messages.subject_clean: [Bug] The Report Option "-R" of featureCounts Generates Invalid Binary Characters
messages.body_plain:
[Bug] The Report Option "-R" of featureCounts Generates Invalid Binary Characters

Version: Subread 1.6.0

OS: Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7.4, macOS 10.13.3

Compiler: Clang 900.0.39.2 in macOS, GCC 7.2.1 in RHEL

Steps:
Supply the "-R" option with SAM or BAM arugment in any normal launch of featureCounts.
The generated detailed read assignment files with the suffix ".featureCounts.sam" or ".featureCounts.bam" contain invalid binary characters, such as 0x00 and 0xFF (may also other invalid characters), right in front of the beginning of the added alignment tag XS, in a format of: [0xFF][0xFF]:[0xFF]:XS:...
These invalid binary characters can be identified in SAM file directly or by converting such BAM files to SAM using Samtools which eneded up with errors.

Reproducibility

This bug can be reproduced everytime when above steps are followed.

messages.subject: Re: [Bug] The Report Option "-R" of featureCounts Generates Invalid Binary Characters
messages.subject_clean: [Bug] The Report Option "-R" of featureCounts Generates Invalid Binary Characters
messages.body_plain:
Thank you for the detailed bug report!

I've found the problem. There is an array-typed tag ("jM:B") in your input SAM file, which has an element type of chars. FeatureCounts had a bug on calculating the sizes of arrays containing chars or short integers -- all the element types were given 4 bytes of memory, while a char should only occupy 1 byte of memory. This bug broke the data structure in featureCounts, making the output SAM file containing wrong tag names.

The bug has been fixed, and the next release should work well on your input SAM files. A quick fix before the next release is to change the type of elements to integer (assuming the tag name is "jM"):

sed -i 's/\tjM:B:c/\tjM:B:i/g' YOUR_SAM_FILE.sam

Thanks,

~Malcolm Cook

messages.subject: feature request: provide parameter to determine where to put outputs of -R reports
messages.subject_clean: feature request: provide parameter to determine where to put outputs of -R reports
messages.body_plain:
I find `featureCounts -R BAM` extraordinarily useful.  I load the .bam files produced in IGV alongside the  feature files and can review the read assignment results in the context of seeing the alignment.  (indeed, IGV lets me group alignments by the XS tag, allowing me to review the alignments by their assignment status - most useful).

However, in my hands, the bam files produced are all placed in the current working directory.  There is no provision for specifying an alternate location, which I think would be most desirable.

Furthermore, I expect there is room for collision if two input files from different directories have the same basename.

I propose that the -R <string> optionally be a path ending in either SAM, BAM, or CORE.  This would be backward compatible with current behavior.

Example:  `-R ./data/subread/assignmentResults/BAM' would produce .bam files in ./data/subread/assignmentResults/

This proposal does not address the potential for collision.  If you agree this is an issue, perhaps there is a better way to avoid the possibility.

If you take on this proposal, I expect you wouldfirst want to address my other request: https://groups.google.com/d/msg/subread/17G_oFNtXDU/VcUadLLJAwAJ

Thanks for subread!

~malcolm

messages.subject: Re: allow relative paths in Rsubread
messages.subject_clean: allow relative paths in Rsubread
messages.body_plain:
Hi Malcolm,

The relative paths are OK for RfeatureCounts. The post that you referred to used "~" in the path, which is not a file-system level abbreviation for "$HOME", but a shell-level abbreviation. Linux shell (eg, bash) or R can replace "~" to the path to your home directory, but RfeatureCounts doesn't do so.

For example, you can use "../../hg19.GTF" as the annotation file, but you cannot use "~/hg19.GTF" -- you should use the home directory in the file names.

Cheers,
Yang

n, thanks for the supporting view and history on this.

Wei, Great news ... I appreciate your efforts...

I put some thought into what that new parameter might be....

You might consider letting the string in

     -R <string>

take on values other than CORE, SAM, BAM

In particular, you could profitably borrow the little language used by Gnu Parallel  OPTIONS <https://www.gnu.org/software/parallel/man.html#OPTIONS>

If you did this, the CORE SAM and BAM could be "aliases" for patterns using the little language.  Like this:

alias          pattern                                  description
CORE      ./{/.}_featurecounts.core        in the current working directory, use the extensionless basename for the current file suffixed with " }_featurecounts.core"
BAM        ./{/.}_featurecounts.bam         in the current working directory, use the extensionless basename for the current file suffixed with " }_featurecounts.bam"
SAM        ./{/.}_featurecounts.sam         in the current working directory, use the extensionless basename for the current file suffixed with " }_featurecounts.sam"

It would also allow lots of flexibility, such as:

pattern              description
{.}_fc.bam         in the same directory as the input file, but with a new suffix of "_fc.bam"
{//}/fc/{/.}.bam    in the 'fc' subdirectory from which the input file came,current working directory, use the basename of the input file with " .bam" extension.
/tmp/fc/$$/{}       in a subfolder of /tmp/fc named after the current process id, at a sub-sub folder mirroring the (possibly relative) folderstructure of the input file

For the last to be most useful, it would be advantageous for featureCounts to create parent directories as needed.

There are probably only a more variations on the above.

Doing this would permit the expressing the options discussed so far, and would be backwards compatible, and would uses a syntax with some history and reasonably broad and considered use.

Woot!
